races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Academy Hurdle
races.verdict: No form on show but WORLD OF THE WAY makes most appeal on paper. Why Wait is well bred for this sphere and can prove the main threat along with Gavin Cromwell's Plumton Queen.

runners.note: Second foal, half-sister to fairly useful hurdler Tir Og (2m-2¼m winner, by Tirwanako), stays 2½m, dam unraced. Wears tongue strap on debut.
Rich History filly, half-sister to fairly useful chaser Gabriel's Getaway and fair hurdler Chosen Judge, with dam's family including high-class chaser Burton Port.
Free Eagle filly. Half-sister to 3 winners, including modest hurdler Abel Mabel who won over 17f. Interesting on pedigree.
Fourth foal, dam, poor maiden hurdler, closely related to smart hurdler/chaser (stayed 4m) Threeunderthrufive. Likely to need time and distance.
Fourth foal, half-sister to 3 winners, including fair 2m hurdle winner Without Burlington (by Without Parole). Dam, ran twice in bumpers, half-sister to fairly useful hurdler (2m winner) Gealach.
First foal, dam unraced half-sister to high-class hurdler/smart chaser (stayed 23f) Zanahiyr and useful hurdle winner around 2m Zariygann. Worth a market check.

Fourth foal, closely related to fair hurdler/chase winner Stanley Stanley (2¾m-3m winner, by Camelot), and half-sister to bumper winner Edmond (by Nathaniel). Dam (b96), bumper winner, half-sister to useful multiple juni

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
races.verdict: KATTY has shown the benefit of her debut effort in 2 starts since, the form of her third at the Curragh last time having been boosted by the winner, and she could be ready to get off the mark. Film Set is feared most as she drops back down in grade, ahead of Formous.

runners.note: €1,900,000 yearling who shaped as if needing the experience when fifth of 21 in maiden over C&D on debut last month. However, was hampered halfway when well held in valuable event at the Curragh (7f) 15 days ago. This ru

Foaled February 18. €2,500 yearling, Dawn Approach filly. Sister to 1m-9.4f winner abroad Mezvirag. Dam, 1¼m-1½m winner, sister to smart 1m-10.7f winner (stayed 1¾m) Paene Magnus. Yard not known for winning 2-y-o newcome

Foaled March 11. €270,000 yearling, Siyouni filly. Half-sister to 2-y-o 7f winner in France Real News. Dam, 2-y-o 6f winner, sister to very smart winner up to 7f Tasleet. Expensive purchase so she's worth a check in the

Foaled April 16. Blue Point filly. Half-sister to smart 1m-10.2f winner Thunder Run. Dam 7f/1m winner out of useful 9.5f winner An Saincheann. Yard's debutants tend to be better for their first experience, though the sta

Knew more than on debut when second in 15-runner maiden over C&D in August. Made little impression upped to Group 3 level when fifth of 8 at the Curragh (7f) 2 weeks ago, but she remains capable of better back in maiden
Showed ability in maidens at this course (5f) and the Curragh (7f) on first 2 starts, but wasn't in the same form when sixth of 8 at Ayr (6f) in August. Could be in the mix back from a break.

€360,000 2-y-o who was sent off favourite on debut, but shaped as if needing the run more than anticipated when fifth of 15 in maiden over this C&D 7 weeks ago. No surprise to see a bold showing this time around.
Foaled April 2. Cotai Glory filly. Dam, French 7f/1m winner, half-sister to useful 7f winner Honey Girl. Trainer 0-5 with 2-y-o newcomers this season.

Attracted support on debut and offered something to work on when sixth of 16 in maiden at Gowran (7f) in September, never nearer having been very slowly away. Promises to take a step forward from that effort.

Some encouragement on debut and has bettered that form in 2 subsequent outings, third of 13 in maiden at the Curragh (the winner runner-up in listed race next time) 15 days ago. Looks to hold strong claims.
Didn't make much impact in 2 maidens in August, eleventh of 14 at Dundalk on latest outing. Looks to be up against it.

Foaled April 1. €300,000 yearling, Minzaal filly. Half-sister to several winners, including smart 9.4f/1¼m winner One For Bobby and useful 5f/6f winner Lam Yai. Dam 7f/1m winner. Makes appeal on paper.
Has shaped as if one for further down the line in 2 maidens so far, again finishing well held when thirteenth of 21 over this C&D 24 days ago.

races.name: DragonBet / EBF Mares' 'National Hunt' Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
races.verdict: PRINCESS DAY proved useful in bumpers last season and is taken to make a successful start over hurdles in the opener. Divine Diva and Kamille Au Kanada may provide the chief threat in what should prove an informative contest.

runners.note: First past the post on both starts in points (disqualified first occasion) and showed a fair bit in a couple of bumpers. Completed a simple task on hurdles bow at Plumpton in May and she remains with potential.
Well backed when making her third start in bumpers a winning one at Newton Abbot in July. However, ran out when remote third on hurdles bow at Warwick last month and looks best watched here.

Joined Jennie Candlish after showing promise on sole start for Fergal O'Brien and won a pair of Sedgefield bumpers earlier this year. Now with new connections and is not taken lightly on switch to hurdling having had a b

Successful on sole outing in Irish points and made a pleasing start under Rules when third of 12 in listed bumper at Cheltenham last November. Reportedly bled when well beaten at Aintree on sole outing since but must be
Just modest form at best in a trio of bumpers but posted promising fourth of 18 in novice at Wincanton (2m) on hurdles bow in February and ought to appreciate this longer trip.

€170,000 purchase after landing an Irish point last spring and looked an excellent prospect in winning first 2 starts in bumpers last winter. Disappointed at Aintree on final outing but looks a big player on hurdles debu

€20,000 3-y-o, £60,000 4-y-o, Walk In The Park mare. Dam lightly raced in bumpers/over hurdles, half-sister to Champion Hurdle winner Katchit and useful hurdler/chaser (stayed 3m) Prince Erik. Easy winner of sole start i

races.name: Co-Op Superstores 3-Y-O Maiden Hurdle
races.verdict: STEP BY STEP showed enough on his Ballinrobe debut 30 days ago to suggest he's capable of winning this, having been awkward early and lost ground at the last before keeping on well in the final stages. Open to improvement second time up, he's preferred to Chairmanforlife, who left his disappointing debut behind when runner-up in conditions company at Listowel last month and can be competitive back

runners.note: A fair 1m winner on the Flat for Joseph Patrick O'Brien but sold for only 6,500 gns after looking less than straightforward at Down Royal on most recent outing in that sphere and little encouragement to be gleaned from e

Dam 2m hurdle winner, also 9.5f-1½m winner on Flat. Showed fairly useful form when winning a 10.5f Cork maiden on heavy ground in the spring. Below that form in a handicap at Royal Ascot and subsequently gelded. One of t
Won 7f handicap at Dundalk in February but showed no aptitude for hurdling on first attempt in July.
Left hurdling debut form when 8½ lengths second of 11 to Danny Power in juvenile event at Listowel last month. Sets the standard on that effort.
Third foal. Well beaten last of 11 in maiden hurdle on debut.
Half-brother to fairly useful hurdler Game Point (winner around 2m, by Blue Point). Fairly useful 7f winner on Flat as a 2-y-o. Market is likely to prove informative.
Half-brother to 2m-2¼m hurdle winner in Italy Spiritofhayton (by Big Bad Bob). Fair maiden on the Flat for Andrew Balding. Makes hurdling debut on first start for new connections (gelded).
Gleneagles gelding. Showed plenty to work on when 1¾ lengths third of 13 to Bell Ex Too in juvenile hurdle at Ballinrobe. Open to improvement and one to consider.
Dam was a fairly useful stayer on the Flat and a half-sister to winning hurdler up to 2¼m Augustive (by Machiavellian) but showed nothing in a quartet of runs on the Flat.
Rich History gelding. Some encouragement when 18 lengths eighth of 13 to Bell Ex Too in juvenile hurdle at Ballinrobe on debut.

Fair maiden on the Flat (bred to stay further than 1m but hasn't done so yet). Has shown aptitude for hurdling when mid-field in 2 juvenile events at Ballinrobe but is probably one for handicaps after another run.

races.name: Alderbrook Handicap (Professional Jump Jockeys) (GBBPlus Race)
races.verdict: A winner on the Flat in France, KLYCOT has developed into a likeable type over hurdles for his current yard and looks interesting upped to 2m for the first time on the level. He gets the vote ahead of Carthusian, who is respected having won both starts for his present stable, with Kotari another to consider.

runners.note: Didn't manage to win for Jessica Harrington in Ireland but made a successful stable debut in handicap at Chester (14.5f) last month. Forged clear when following up at Ffos Las (2m) 2 weeks ago, so he's not taken lightly

Fairly useful winner on the Flat (raced up to 1½m) in France and similar form as a juvenile hurdler for current yard, scoring twice before a good third in the Fred Winter at Cheltenham in March. Makes plenty of appeal up

Much improved for current yard with 6 wins since December, successful over this C&D in May before going on to complete the 4-timer at Lingfield (all-weather). Shaped as if possibly amiss when down the field at Newcastle

5-time winner at this venue, with his latest success over C&D in June last year. Yet to fully fire this year, including over hurdles the last twice, but he's now 5 lb below his last winning mark so isn't one to be ruled

Doubled her tally at Southwell (1½m) on return in March and runner-up 3 times since, including over this C&D in May. However, has run below form the last twice, returning from 13 weeks off when down the field here (1¾m)

Without a win campaigned back on the Flat this year but arrives in decent heart, creditable fourth of 10 at Salisbury (1¾m) 10 days ago. Can give his running once more trying this trip for the first time on the level.

Completed a hat-trick with success on the turf at Lingfield (16.5f) in June and has looked back in form on his last 2 starts, fourth of 6 at Newmarket (2¼m) 22 days ago. Remains 6 lb above his last winning mark, though d

Not straightforward but was runner-up in this race in 2024 before landing the prize last year. However, he ran below form on final outing in 2025, before falling over hurdles at Sandown in January. Has 9-month absence to

Successful twice on the Flat this season, winning at Doncaster (1½m) in June and in 3-runner contest at Pontefract (17f) in August. Making first start since leaving Brian Ellison, ran well when third of 8 at Kempton (2m)

Landed back-to-back all-weather handicaps early last year but not in the same form in his 2 starts on the Flat since, the latest when sixth of 8 at Kempton in August. Did score over hurdles prior to that, but fell early

Ran better than for a while when close fifth of 8 at Bath (1¾m) in June and, after a lesser effort over hurdles, soon returned to form when runner-up at Haydock 16 days ago. Represents last year's winning yard and enters

Dual winner last autumn and worked his way back to form this season when narrowly denied at Salisbury (1½m) in May. A couple of below-par efforts followed, but got back on track when 2¼ lengths fifth of 12 at Bath (1¾m)

races.name: Tifrums Irish EBF (C & G) Maiden
races.verdict: Aidan O'Brien probably holds the aces here with BENGAL TIGER taken to put his experience to good use having chased home a next-time-out improver over C&D 3 weeks ago. Market confidence behind stablemate Major Triumph would put a slightly different slant on things, while Rejoinder could be a different proposition this time.

runners.note: A lot sharper with cheekpieces fitted on second start when runner-up in a C&D maiden 24 days ago. In top hands and he sets the standard with Moore presumably choosing him over well-bred stablemate Major Triumph.
Foaled January 25. €24,000 yearling, Persian Force gelding. Half-brother to several winners, including useful 7f-8.3f winner Sir Guy Porteous and 2-y-o 6f winner Velveteen. Dam maiden (stayed 1m).

Foaled February 7. No Nay Never colt. Dam, 2-y-o 7f/1m winner who stayed 1½m, half-sister to smart French 10.4f-1¾m winner Jannah Flower. Newcomer for leading connections and market may well tell the tale in relation to
Foaled March 29. €52,000 yearling, Sioux Nation colt. Dam French 6f winner out of smart winner up to 1¼m (2-y-o 1m winner) Sparkling Beam.

Foaled March 10. 110,000 gns yearling, €68,000 2-y-o, Mehmas colt. Brother to useful 2-y-o 5f/6f winner Ballistic Missile. Limited short-term promise starting out on heavy ground at the Curragh 2 weeks ago.

€82,000 2-y-o. Space Blues colt. Closely related to useful winner up to 1m Thunder Beauty and half-brother to 3 winners, including useful 1½m winner Haku. Dam German 11f/1½m winner. Found it tough going in listed compan
Foaled March 22. $180,000 yearling, Golden Pal colt. Dam unraced out of smart winner up to 6f (including Queen Mary Stakes at 2 yrs) Acapulco. Of obvious interest on debut.
Foaled March 17. €75,000 yearling, Persian Force gelding. Half-brother to 2-y-o 6.5f winner in Poland Birnbaum Warrior. Dam, 5.3f/6f winner, half-sister to useful 6f winner Berkshire Whisper.

races.name: DragonBet Daily Extra Place Handicap Hurdle
races.verdict: Preference is for UGO BINGO, who has been cut plenty of slack by the handicapper and ran well in a similar contest at Newton Abbot last time. Little Pi and Kates Choice head the list of dangers.

runners.note: Ran with promise when fourth in novice hurdle at Worcester (16f) on NH debut in September of last year but not really built on that since. May do better now sent handicapping.

Ex-Irish mare who capitalised on a reduced mark to win a 7-runner handicap hurdle at Ffos Las (2½m, good to soft) in May. Posted creditable third in follow-up bid at Fontwell 3 weeks later and warrants respect on return
No impact in a trio of starts over hurdles and been out of sorts on the Flat of late. Hard to fancy.

Back to winning ways over this trip at Huntingdon in February and made the frame on next 2 outings, including when respectable third of 6 in handicap hurdle at Ludlow the following month. Fairly treated on return and mus
Runner-up in a bumper on debut last summer. Modest form over hurdles, though, and ran poorly on debut for new yard at Fontwell last month.

Point winner who hasn't stood much racing since a promising maiden Rules season in 2023. Offered more than on return when sixth of 10 in handicap hurdle at Worcester (2½m, good to soft, 9/1) 31 days ago but shapes as tho

Not scored since 2024 but has dropped to a handy mark and arrives on back of creditable third of 10 in handicap hurdle at Newton Abbot (2¼m, good to firm) 50 days ago. Yard had a winner/second from 3 runners at this meet

Clearly been one with issues since winning bumper/maiden for Olly Murphy earlier in his career. Standout effort last season when runner-up in soft-ground handicap chase at Ffos Las in April. Hard to be confident back hur
Had a productive year on the Flat, scoring 3 times. Run poorly all 4 starts over hurdles back in 2024 but he figures off a handy mark if able to convert this year's Flat form into this sphere.

Steady improvement in maiden/novice company and posted respectable efforts in handicap hurdles last year, including when fourth of 8 in handicap hurdle at Stratford 16 months ago. Not seen since, though.
Resumed his progress in first-time tongue tie when landing 8-runner handicap hurdle at Market Rasen in July but not really built on that since. Others appeal more. Had breathing operation.
Runner-up both starts in Irish points but unable to trouble the judge in 4 starts over hurdles earlier this year. Can start handicapping from a lowly mark at least. Hood on first time.
Posted his best effort when fifth over this sort of trip at Ffos Las in November but no impact in either start subsequently and not seen since February. Others more convincing.
Well held only start in bumpers and similar story thus far over hurdles, including on handicap bow at Sedgefield in April. Makes limited appeal.

races.name: Kendellen Construction Handicap Hurdle (0-100)
races.verdict: LET HIM B bounced back to form when runner-up at Roscommon 13 days ago and is taken to go one better for a yard in good form. Boola Times returned to his best with O’Keeffe back in the saddle at Wexford in August and should remain competitive despite a 6 lb rise, while Gortmore Lady was collared only late at Perth last time and can be involved if repeating that effort.

runners.note: Bumper winner but has shown only modest form over hurdles and fences since. Distant third in handicap chase at Wexford last time.

Inconsistent sort who got off the mark when landing a 14-runner 2½m Wexford handicap in August. Attracted support that day and, while a 6 lb rise makes life harder, he ought to be thereabouts if giving his running.
Has shown little to be enthused about of late, both over hurdles and on the Flat. Has dropped to last winning mark as a result but requires a big leap of faith.

Prominent in the betting and bounced back to form when 4½ lengths second of 16 to Getaway Charlie at Roscommon last month. Back up 2 lb but looks sure to make his presence felt now back up and running.

Placed twice in mares maidens last season but offered little on the back of a 5-month break when well beaten in a handicap at Roscommon last time. Needs to bounce back and probably find some improvement to boot.
Little impact in handicap hurdles and recent exploits don't suggest that is likely to change now.

Long-standing maiden over hurdles. Looked rusty returning from a 14-month absence when mid-division in handicap at Galway in September. Races from a career-low mark and shouldn't be inconvenienced by the marked drop in t
Still looking for a breakthrough success. Ran better than for a while when third of 14 in mares handicap at Wexford in August but has failed to build on that in 2 starts since.
Some promise in his qualifying runs but failed to improve on first foray into handicap and now has something to prove.

Dual winner over hurdles. Creditable third of 16 in handicap hurdle at Tipperary (16.9f, good to soft) last spring before running poorly at Wexford. Makes debut for new connections now returning from 15-month absence.
Placed once from 3 starts in bumpers and stand out effort over hurdles when third of 8 in Worcester maiden last season. Wears blinkers on debut for new yard.
No show in maiden hurdles, off 15 months prior to return.
Turned in best effort this season when ¾-length second of 12 to Coventry at Perth last month. First-time blinkers replace cheekpieces and entitled to be in the mix if repeating that performance.
Maiden who placed off higher marks than this last season but hasn't fired this season and unlikely to be of interest unless market was to speak in his favour.
Good efforts when placed last 2 starts, 8 lengths second of 12 to Might Be The One at Downpatrick on latest. Should be suited by the step back up in trip
Won during the winter and was placed in the spring, but her form has tailed off of late and is hard to recommend as a result.

races.name: Virgin Bet / British EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
races.verdict: BRYNMAIR GOLD made a promising start when a strong-finishing second at Kempton and he appeals as the type who can improve markedly from his first outing. He is taken to get the better of Cornichon, who also shaped encouragingly on debut when making the frame at Newbury, while War Chest could be thereabouts once more.

runners.note: Showed promise amidst inexperience when fourth of 15 in maiden at Newbury (War Chest ahead in second) on debut 23 days ago, faring best of the group that raced near side. In good hands and can make his presence felt with
Little promise in a pair of maidens 4 months apart (gelded in the interim), again failing to beat a rival in 14-runner event at Newmarket (7f) 16 days ago.

Showed a fair amount of ability when third in an Ascot novice on debut and ran to a similar level when runner-up in 15-runner maiden at Newbury 23 days ago. Helped by being well positioned last time, but he merits consid

Shaped well on debut when second of 10 in novice at Kempton 11 days ago, beaten by only a neck having finished with a flourish. Yard's 2-y-os tend to come on plenty for their first run, so he rates as a likely contender.
Foaled April 9. 2,000 gns 2-y-o, Tasleet gelding. Dam 6f winner (including at 2 yrs). Worth a market check with yard having a winner and one placed from a trio of 2-y-o newcomers last month.

Held back by inexperience on his first start, though the penny was dropping late when never-nearer fifth of 10 in maiden at Bath (5f) in May. Has something to find in this contest as he goes up in trip after 5 months off
Foaled March 6. 7,500 gns yearling, Tasleet gelding. Half-brother to 6f winner Margorie. Dam 2-y-o 5.7f winner who stayed 1m. Trainer 0-9 with 2-y-o debutants this season.
Sent off at big odds (150/1) for her first start and was always behind when eleventh of 15 in maiden at Newbury last month. Looks to be up against it.

races.name: Irish EBF Auction Series Race Final
races.verdict: WHOSINTERVIEWINWHO looks the pick of the weights and can open his account at the expense of the class-dropping The Scallionator. Letmeentertainyou also makes each-way appeal in this valuable contest.

runners.note: Much improved when impressively getting off the mark in nursery at Galway (7f, soft) in July and backed it up when second in conditions race at Roscommon. In first-time cheekpieces, below form eighth of 17 in valuable ev

Fairly useful colt. 14/1, showed improved form when winning 15-runner maiden at Cork (1m, good to soft) in August, suited by increase in trip. Blinkers go on for the first time and needs to progress again dropping back t

Fairly useful form. Much improved to get off the mark in 7-runner minor event (25/1) at Listowel (1m, good to soft) by 1¾ lengths from Romance 19 days ago, suited by the way the race developed. Place claims.
Progressive filly who opened her account in 15-runner maiden over C&D (good to soft) 24 days ago by ½ length from Dawnmore, having to pick way through. Further improvement required to be involved.

Offered plenty to work on when second of 17 in maiden at Fairyhouse on debut in June but failed to immediately build on that at Navan next time. Proved a let down last time and needs the fitting of cheekpieces to bring a

Highly tried after winning a maiden at Listowel in May. Travelled well/didn't need to improve when making all in 6f conditions race at Cork last month before being found out in a listed race there last time. Entitled to

Fairly useful filly who relished the step up to 1m to get off the mark on nursery debut at Killarney by 3¼ lengths from Maggie Walker. 3/1, career best when winning 6-runner nursery at Killarney (1m, good) in August. Ton
Didn't have to improve when off the mark at the third attempt in maiden at Roscommon in May but form is just ordinary. Has absence to overcome but booking of Lee a plus.
Made all when winning Leopardstown maiden in August. Third both starts since and this demands more. Booking of Keane a plus.
Lightly-raced maiden who's run to a fair level on each of his 4 starts, latest when second of 14 at Thurles (8.3f, good to soft, 11/8) 3 days ago.

Speedily-bred colt who showed promise on his first 2 outings, his debut run at the Curragh having worked out very well in particular. Has since finished well held and can only be watched at present. Tongue strap goes on.
Has run to just a modest level at best in 3 maidens. Has plenty on his plate at the weights and may be one for low-grade handicaps. Cheekpieces added.

Well backed and much improved when second in maiden at Galway in August, but ran no sort of race at Down Royal next time. Resumed progress fitted with a first-time visor when 1¾ lengths second of 6 to Pink Venom on nurse

races.name: DragonBet / EBF 'National Hunt' Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
races.verdict: The market will no doubt be a decent guide as to what's expected but LION ROSE SIVOLA is selected to make a successful return/hurdling debut having found just one too strong in a couple of soft ground bumpers last season. Dan Skelton has unleashed plenty of runners this week and debutant Skibidirizz is put forward as the main danger, with standard-setter Mwabani taken to fill out third on his reap

runners.note: £100,000 buy after winning sole start in Irish points and looked likely to follow up for much of the straight on his Rules debut in a C&D bumper last November. Shaped well again at Kelso subsequently only to tie up and g

Well beaten in a couple of Punchestown bumpers earlier in the year (sent off short-priced favourite on debut). Has joined another top stable ahead of this hurdling debut and interesting to see what the market makes of hi

Plenty of promise when runner-up all 3 starts in junior events last season, though turned over at odds on for a second time when last seen at Exeter (17f, good) in March. Has more to offer in this sphere and should be ba
€38,000 3-y-o, Yeats gelding. Half-brother to fairly useful hurdler Allavina and fair hurdler One Cool Scorpion. Dam unraced. Tongue tied for debut. Market check advised.
Beaumec De Houelle gelding who showed precious little in juvenile hurdle at Bangor (17f, heavy) on debut last November. Given time since but looks one for low-grade handicaps further down the line.
Workforce gelding. Dam unraced sister to useful hurdler/chaser (stayed 21f) I'm A Game Changer. Of obvious interest on debut.

races.name: Connolly's RED MILLS Irish EBF Auction & Median Maiden Hurdle
races.verdict: MARTYMILL has long since looked a stayer in the making and should be suited by the return to more galloping track second time up over hurdles. Conor'salwaysright also managed to win in bumpers and looks the main danger on hurdling debut, while Square Jasmin sets the standard on his sole previous hurdling start and should also be involved.

runners.note: Suited by the emphasis on stamina when off the mark in bumpers at the sixth attempt at Downpatrick in August but didn't quite match that level of form faced with a sharp 2½m when 13 lengths third of 9 to Nightflyer in ma
Arctic Cosmos gelding. Unplaced on completed start in points and well beaten in maiden at Listowel on hurdling debut.
Hinted at ability on second of 2 starts in bumpers but has shown little in 2 starts in maiden hurdles.
Kew Gardens gelding. Stepped up on bumper debut when winning 8-runner 2¼m event at Sligo in August. Will be suited by this longer trip now hurdling and looks one for the shortlist.
From the family of Queen Mother Champion Chase winner Put The Kettle On. Dead-heated for third completed start in points and has looked one for the longer term on both outings over hurdles.

Hunter's Light gelding. Offered something to work on when fourth of 16 in a juvenile hurdle at Cork (17f) on debut in May and made the frame again switched to a bumper at Wexford last time. Returns to hurdling and sets t
€8,000 3-y-o. Order Of St George gelding. Last to finish both completed starts in points, pulled last time (Mar 2026).

Made the frame once from 4 starts in bumpers and stepped up on hurdling debut when 9½ lengths third of 6 to Myluckymaker in maiden at Fairyhouse. Steps up in trip and will need to brush up her jumping if she's to do any

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Nursery (GBBPlus Race)
races.verdict: CASHINOROYALE took a big step forward when runner-up at Kempton and his opening mark may underestimate him with further progress likely. Zarak Crown is the obvious threat having won a decent novice at Ayr, while Lots Road also has potential.

runners.note: From a Group-winning French family and left his debut well behind to win Ayr novice by a short head. That form has already started to work out and he almost certainly has more to offer.
Off the mark at the third attempt in 7f Epsom maiden in July. Went close at Epsom following month before out of her depth in valuable event at Goodwood. Step up in trip likely to suit.
Price went the right way in the sales ring, and she left first 2 starts well behind when just edged out by a newcomer in Sandown maiden, clear of rest. Opening mark looks a fair one.
Too Darn Hot colt who took a step forward when third in Haydock novice last month, putting experience to good use. Beaten almost 7 lengths that day but the form has since been boosted.
Third in 7f novices at Thirsk and Newbury this summer but was never a threat on nursery bow at latter track last time despite running to form. Step up in trip will at least suit.

52,000 gns 2-y-o by Palace Pier who stepped up on debut when second at Kempton, no match for a useful prospect. Opening mark looks a handy one and extra 1f is expected to suit to he has plenty in his favour.
Debut 6f Haydock winner in May. Went close under a penalty at Ffos Las following month but has regressed since.
Has needed the experience on all 3 starts (in barely a month). In very good hand and type to do better now qualified and up in trip.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Garnet Stakes (Fillies' And Mares' Listed)
races.verdict: Preference is for PRINCESS CHILD, who knuckled down well when second at the Curragh last time and will appreciate the return to this longer trip. English raider Queen's Reign and the in-form Rebel Wave are also of interest.

runners.note: Back from 5 months off when very good fourth of 11 in listed race at Listowel (1m, good to soft) 19 days ago, needing stiffer test. Cheekpieces back on. Others hold stronger claims.
Most progressive last season, winning 3 of her 4 starts. Not as good this year, racing too freely when eighth over longer trip at Gowran last month but must enter calculations.
Winner of Naas maiden and handicap at Navan in August last year. Yet to really fire this season, though, and looks up against it here.

Dual winner in August last year, including a Tipperary Group 3. Yet to score this season but shaped well when second of 10 in Concorde Stakes at the Curragh (7f, soft, 11/1) 7 days ago and ought to appreciate the return
Useful winner in France, notably a listed race at Fontainebleau (1¼m, good to soft) last November. May have needed belated reappearance for new stable last month. This should reveal more.

Placed in 3 listed events last season. Restricted to just 2 outings this season but back to somewhere near her best when third of 13 in listed race at Baden-Baden (7f, soft) 40 days ago. One of likelier contenders.
Dual handicap winner at Gowran earlier this year. Been a mixed bag since, though, and looks up against it here. Hood on first time.

races.verdict: This looks between penalised winners PASSENGER, Ifuknowuknow and Rokanako, and they are preferred in that order.

races.verdict: She may not have won this year, but NAVY WATERS has held her form really well this campaign. Having finished with more to give at Down Royal recently, Willie McCreery's mare is put forward as the answer. Vanir finished runner-up in that same race, so she rates as an obvious danger, with last-time-out winner Letiza rounding off the shortlist in an open-looking finale.
